subject: Artificial Intelligence
chapters: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms

questions.text: Differentiate between Natural (Human) Intelligence and Artificial Intelligence. Can AI replace humans? Justify your stance.
Discuss the role of Artificial Intelligence in public service delivery in the context of Nepal.

What is an Intelligent Agent? Do we need PEAS for designing an intelligent agent? Design the PEAS (Performance Measure, Environment, Actuators, Sensors) framework for an Automated Robot in a manufacturing plant.
Explain different types of Intelligent Agent architectures (Simple Reflex, Model-Based, Goal-Based, Utility-Based) with examples.
Can machine think? Explain your stance with appropriate reasons. Relate it with Turing Test and Reverse Turing Test.
What is cognition and learning? Why are they important in AI? Explain the factors that are responsible for learning.
Mention the problem formulation of 8-Queen problem as a state space search with one appropriate solution.
Solve the Crypt-Arithmetic problem: LOGIC + LOGIC = PROLOG by showing all required letter-to-digit assignment steps.
What are criteria for defining a problem in AI? Solve the Crypt-Arithmetic problem: BASE + BALL = GAMES showing all steps.

List down characteristics of a well-defined problem. Solve the 2-Jugs Problem (5-litre and 3-litre jugs with no markings and a pump) to measure exactly 1 liter of water by specifying states and production rules.
Define well-defined problem. Solve the Crypt-Arithmetic problem: ONE + ONE + TWO = FOUR by showing all steps.
What do you mean by Constraints Satisfaction Problem (CSP)? List all constraints and solve the Crypt-Arithmetic problem: EAT + THAT = APPLE.
Explain steps of problem solving with suitable example. Solve the Crypt-Arithmetic algorithm: SWIM + WEAR = RELAX.
Solve the Crypt-Arithmetic problem by defining it as a production system: TWO + TWO = FOUR.
What are the dimensions to evaluate search algorithms (Completeness, Time Complexity, Space Complexity, Optimality)? Explain how informed search is different from uninformed search.
Why is searching important in problem solving? Differentiate between Depth First Search (DFS), Breadth First Search (BFS), and Depth Limited Search (DLS) with their performance criteria.

Explain $A^*$ Search Algorithm ($f(n) = g(n) + h(n)$). How does $A^*$ search overcome problems associated with Greedy Best-First Search? Trace $A^*$ and greedy search on a given graph with heuristic costs.

What are the drawbacks of the Min-Max algorithm for two-player game playing? Explain how Alpha-Beta Pruning overcomes its limitations, and trace Alpha-Beta pruning on a given game tree to identify pruned branches.
What are the drawbacks of Hill Climbing search (Local Maxima, Ridges, Plateau)? Explain how the Simulated Annealing algorithm escapes local maxima.
When shall we use Genetic Algorithms (GA)? Explain all steps in GA including Selection (Roulette wheel, Tournament), Crossover, and Mutation operations with a block diagram.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Define Production System. Differentiate between Forward Chaining and Backward Chaining in rule-based inference with suitable examples.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Axioms: "The law says it is a crime for an American to sell weapons to hostile nations. Country Nono, an enemy of America, has some missiles, and all missiles were sold to it by Colonel West, who is American." Prove that Colonel West is a criminal using FOPL Resolution Refutation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Axioms: "Every child loves Santa. Everyone who loves Santa loves any reindeer. Rudolph is a reindeer, and Rudolph has a red nose. Anything which has a red nose is weird or is a clown. No reindeer is a clown. Scrooge does not love anything which is weird." Prove: "Scrooge is not a child" using Resolution Refutation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Axioms: "Every country that has weapons and is hostile is dangerous. Every country that is an enemy of America is hostile. Kadon is a country. Kadon has weapons. Kadon is an enemy of America. Any dangerous country should be sanctioned." Prove: "Kadon should be sanctioned" using Resolution Refutation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Axioms: "All people who are not poor and are smart are happy. Those people who can read are not stupid. John can read and is wealthy. Happy people have exciting lives." Prove: "Can anyone be found with an exciting life?" using Resolution Refutation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Axioms: "Everyone who loves all animals is loved by someone. Anyone who kills an animal is loved by no one. Jack loves all animals. Either Jack or Curiosity killed the cat." Prove: "Did Curiosity kill the cat?" using Resolution Refutation.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Axioms: "Steve only likes easy courses. Science courses are hard. All courses in basket weaving department are easy. BK301 is a basket weaving course." Prove that Steve likes BK301 course using Resolution Refutation Method.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Explain Conceptual Dependency (CD) and Scripts in knowledge representation. Convert sentences into Semantic Network: (a) Average height of adult is 5'6", (b) Cricket player is adult male, (c) Adult male is a person, (d) Batting average of cricket player is 37.59, (e) Rohit Paudel is a Batsman / Fielder, (f) Batsman is a cricket player, (g) Rohit Paudel is Captain / Team is Nepal.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Define Semantic Networks and Frames. Represent given facts into a Semantic Network: Cat is a mammal, Bear is a mammal, Whale lives in water, Fish is an animal / Ram likes Jhilke, Jhilke is a cat.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: An individual has 3 different email accounts (#1: 70%, #2: 20%, #3: 10% messages). Spam rates are 1% for #1, 2% for #2, and 5% for #3. What is the probability that a randomly selected spam message is from account #2?

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: In a population 1% of people have a certain genetic defect. 90% of tests detect the defect (true positive), and 9.6% detect positive even without defect. If a person gets a positive test result, what is the probability they actually have the genetic defect?

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Three factories produce light bulbs: Factory A (50%), Factory B (30%), Factory C (20%). Defective rates are 2% for A, 3% for B, and 4% for C. If a randomly selected bulb is found defective, what is the probability it was produced by Factory B?

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: What is Prior Probability and Posterior Probability and show how these probabilities are used in Bayes' Theorem? Explain how reasoning is done in a Bayesian Belief Network.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: Why CNF is necessary? "Everyone who loves all animals are loved by someone" — represent this statement in FOPL and explain all steps involved to convert it into CNF.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Knowledge Representation and Probabilistic Reasoning
questions.text: What is Fuzzy Logic? When do we use it? Explain Fuzzy Inference Systems (Fuzzification, Membership Functions, Fuzzy Rules, Defuzzification) with a suitable example.
What is Reinforcement Learning? Explain Agent, Environment, State, Action, Reward, Policy, and Q-learning with real-world examples.
How is the best attribute selected in the ID3 Decision Tree algorithm using Entropy and Information Gain?
Define Machine Learning. Differentiate between Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning paradigms with examples.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: Given a neural network with weights a, b, c, d, e, f where hidden layer computes $h_1 = \max(c \cdot x_1 + e \cdot x_2, 0)$ and $h_2 = \max(d \cdot x_1 + f \cdot x_2, 0)$, and inputs $x_1=-1, x_2=-1$, weights $a=1, b=1, c=4, d=7, e=2, f=2$. Perform forward propagation and update weights for second hidden layer for $a$ and $b$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: Explain the McCulloch-Pitts model of a neuron with a diagram. Explain how to choose the best activation function (Sigmoid, ReLU, Tanh) for a particular project.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: When do we need a Hopfield Neural Network? Make a comparison between Feed-Forward Networks and Hopfield Neural Networks.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: What is a Perceptron? Show that a single perceptron is not sufficient to realize a network behaving as an XOR gate (Linear Separability problem).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: What is a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)? When do we need the Error Backpropagation Algorithm? Explain with an example.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Neural Networks and Deep Learning Algorithms
questions.text: Using Hebbian Learning Algorithm, construct a neural network that behaves as an AND gate. Is Hebbian learning a supervised method? Justify.
Explain the different levels of linguistic analysis in Natural Language Processing (NLP: Phonological, Morphological, Syntactic, Semantic, Pragmatic). Provide examples for each level.
What are the problems and ambiguities associated with NLP? List down the different steps involved in Natural Language Processing with suitable examples.

You are hired by a company to work on a Nepali Language Chatbot / NLP product. What are the knowledge bases and challenges associated with Nepali language? Describe your plan to mitigate them with a block diagram.

Define Expert System and Expert System Shells. Draw the architecture block diagram of an Expert System, explain its components (Knowledge Base, Inference Engine, Explanation Facility), and discuss its benefits and limitations.
What is Computer Vision / Machine Vision? Create a scenario where Machine Vision is required (e.g. automated inspection). List down the steps and applications of Machine Vision.
Discuss modern transformer-based architectures, Self-Attention mechanisms, and Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) conversational models in AI.
Explain Federated Learning and how it preserves data privacy during distributed model training.
Discuss Ethics in AI, AI Bias, Explainable AI (XAI), and the socio-economic challenges of deploying AI products in Nepal.
